newsitem.title: USA: Costs from IBM bomb threat hard to assess.
newsitem.headline: Costs from IBM bomb threat hard to assess.

text.p: As police continued their search on Wednesday, officials at International Business Machines Corp said it would be difficult to assess the cost of closing a company semiconductor manufacturing plant.
The Burlington Free Press Wednesday quoted an IBM spokesman as saying it would cost the company $1 million a day, but another IBM spokesman told Reuters the number was "very speculative."
"There's just no way to know at this moment," spokesman Thomas Beermann said.

Police evacuated the plant late Tuesday and continued to search the building on Wednesday, after receiving a telephone call from an unidentified male who warned a bomb would explode at a certain time.
Beermann said he did not know how long the plant would stay closed. The plant employs as many as 7,000 workers and is Vermont's largest private employer.
"The search is ongoing. I don't really have any more information beyond that," he said.
The facility operates around the clock, seven days a week, and is one of IBM's important chip manufacturing centers, Beermann said.
Bomb-sniffing dogs from Connecticut and Vermont were called in and were searching the plant, located in a suburb of Burlington, police said.
